Target-scope guard: the ulnar-neuropathy target identity is generic; the elbow evidence base concerns ulnar neuropathy at the cubital tunnel, so the anatomic concordance (medial epicondyle borders the cubital tunnel) is recorded as an edge guard and non-cubital ulnar presentations are excluded from the pathway.
governanceNotes: D1 batch 29 (2026-09-23): one bounded ulnar-neuropathy association authored from the medial-epicondyle coexistence literature (coexistence with ulnar neuropathy at the cubital tunnel documented across decades of elbow literature; Kim 2021 shear-wave elastography documents mechanical nerve abnormality at the tunnel; Zanesco 2025 elbow epidemiology and Khouja 2024 occupational-disease series document both conditions as the dominant elbow diagnoses); the shared-mechanical-environment confound (repetitive elbow loading drives both) and the generic-identity anatomic-scope guard are recorded.

No rotator-cuff or radial-neuropathy edge was authored: the rotator-cuff literature is shoulder-population based without epicondylitis-specific association data, and radial neuropathy co-occurrence with lateral epicondylitis lacks quantitative association studies (searches returned none); both pathways are recorded here rather than left unexamined.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Ulnar neuropathy at the cubital tunnel co-occurs with medial epicondylitis at substantially elevated rates across the elbow literature (coexistence documented as a classic clinical association), Kim 2021's shear-wave elastography work demonstrates stiffer nerve mechanics in cubital-tunnel neuropathy consistent with mechanical irritation at the tunnel bordered by the medial epicondyle, and the Zanesco 2025 (847-patient) and Khouja 2024 (431-case) elbow-disease series document medial epicondylitis and ulnar-nerve syndrome as the dominant medial-elbow diagnoses in the same populations.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation is established at the mapping level: the shared-mechanical-environment confound (repetitive flexion, valgus loading, and elbow-use occupation drive both conditions and can co-produce them without either causing the other), swelling or inflammatory infiltrate from epicondylitis compressing the adjacent nerve is anatomically plausible but not individually demonstrable, and the generic target identity spans cubital-tunnel and more proximal or distal ulnar lesions that lack the anatomic relationship.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: A hypothesized adjacent-structure compression pathway: medial-epicondyle flexor-pronator inflammation and swelling increase pressure within the cubital tunnel immediately posterior to the epicondyle, and repetitive valgus strain of the epicondylitis phenotype mechanically irritates the ulnar nerve against the tunnel roof, producing paresthesia and weakness in the ulnar distribution; individual attribution requires electrodiagnostic localization of the lesion to the cubital tunnel with compatible chronology.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The coexistence is classic and the anatomy adjacent, but the literature does not quantify an epicondylitis-attributable fraction of ulnar neuropathy and the shared-exposure confound is strong; neuropathy must be electrodiagnostically localized to the cubital tunnel rather than assumed from ulnar symptoms, and pre-existing neuropathy, cervical radiculopathy, and systemic neuropathies must be excluded; no probability estimate is asserted.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: Documented medial or lateral epicondylitis by examination or imaging; electrodiagnostically confirmed ulnar neuropathy localized at or near the cubital tunnel with compatible chronology; exclusion of cervical radiculopathy, thoracic-outlet compression, and systemic or hereditary neuropathy; occupational and recreational loading review shared by both conditions; orthopedic and neurology assessment of the individual relationship
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: Ulnar nerve subluxation or dislocation with independent cause
Prior elbow trauma or arthrosis causing tunnel narrowing independent of tendinopathy
